text:
Sampled rankings can reverse model comparisons, even in expectation ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)); a [2025 study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) further examines sampling fidelity and robustness. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds aggregate accuracy hides head/mid/tail disparities and random-negative training favors head items. Diagnostic implication: compare identical permitted training-prefix targets under uniform-sampled, popularity-matched, hard-negative and full-catalog unseen-item rankings. Define frequency bands using training counts only; report paired differences with user-cluster bootstrap intervals. Keep pinned validation HR@10 unchanged. Hard negatives measure discrimination under difficult candidate sets; unobserved items are not verified dislikes.

[Balancing Embedding Spectrum (2024 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12032) connects pairwise-learning dynamics to dimensional collapse, with experiments on MF/LightGCN. Effective rank, exp(−Σpᵢ log pᵢ), using normalized singular values, measures spectral concentration and is invariant to global rescaling. Proposed GRU adaptation: measure item embeddings and final nonpadding states separately, exclude padding, document centering, and repeat within frequency bands. Low rank establishes geometric concentration; it does not establish a GRU failure or prove that increasing rank improves recommendations.

[Recurrent-gradient analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v28/pascanu13.pdf) provides a mechanistic basis for lag-wise gradient/Jacobian probes. Proposed GRU controls: measure final-state sensitivity to earlier inputs, clipping frequency, and prediction changes after prefix truncation or order shuffling that preserves item counts and the last item. Pair gradients with behavioral changes: negligible gradients alone cannot distinguish useful forgetting from failed memory. Frequency-matched comparisons and unchanged-popularity perturbations strengthen interpretation, but the cited evidence does not establish this complete suite as a validated causal diagnostic for GRU4Rec.
